A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEMANTICQA research and contain 24 readable pages. The main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, supervised baseline experiments and human performance measurements, including results in Tables 3–7 and appendix Tables 10, 12 and 13.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and human measurements in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The benchmark task formulations, unified prompting, sequential compositions and Oracle Schema procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices C–D.

E1.justification: Table 1 and Appendix B retain the same English datasets and ten task types covering idioms, lexical collocations, noun compounds and verbal multiword expressions.

E2.justification: The evaluated language models, BERT/T5 baselines, human comparisons and random/majority baselines are unchanged. Revised model citations in Section 4.1 do not alter comparator membership.

E3.justification: Data preparation, metrics, zero-/three-/five-shot settings, category-scaling procedures and human evaluation protocols are unchanged. The BERTScore citation changes from 2019 to 2020 without changing the metric.

E4.justification: Both retain the same in-context learning analyses, semantic category scaling, sequential-task evaluations, Oracle Schema comparison and appendix confusion matrix. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 10–11 retain seeds 21, 42 and 84; Tables 10 and 13 retain their repeated-run and standard-deviation reporting. Figure 5 still reports variation across tasks within each category.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 7 retains DeepSeek-R1's zero-shot accuracy of 51.6% without Oracle Schema and 64.1% with it.

T1.justification: The formal task definitions, input/output formulation and lexical-function definitions are unchanged. Table 9 changes two source citations while retaining the corresponding definitions and descriptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about operation-aligned semantic evaluation, controlled prompting and diagnostic evaluation of sequential-task failures.

C2.justification: Interpretations of metric sensitivity, human comparisons and workflow brittleness are unchanged. The limitations retain the same English-only scope, incomplete phrase coverage and restrictions on task compositions.

D1.justification: Appendices B–F retain the same preprocessing instructions, prompts, decoding parameters, hardware, training hyperparameters and annotation guidance. Benchmark code and dataset access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: GPT-5 and Gemini references are replaced with system-card and technical-report citations. Table 9 replaces Fontenelle's 1997 book with Thielen's 1999 review for IncepPredPlus and CausPredMinus. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits chiefly update citation wording, author and publication metadata, bibliography entries and the version/date banner. The substantive prose and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 has small alignment and spacing adjustments. Updated citations cause local text wrapping and bibliography reflow. Figure and table membership, plot content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Fuller model references and publication metadata improve source identification. However, Table 9 replaces an original book citation with a review, and the supplied PDFs do not establish whether that replacement supports the two definitions. With the scientific content otherwise unchanged, the net quality effect of these referencing changes is uncertain.
